# Template source built from HTTP request data (Python)

`qualor:python/template-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-1336](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1336.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data that becomes the source of a Jinja or Django template: Flask's
`render_template_string()`, `jinja2.Template()`, `Environment.from_string()` (also Flask's
`app.jinja_env` and Starlette's `Jinja2Templates`), Django's `Template()` and
`engines[...].from_string()`. Request data passed as context values is fine and not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A template is code. With Jinja, an expression such as `{{ cycler.__init__.__globals__.os }}` walks
from template objects to Python modules and runs commands on the server; Django templates can read
the application's objects and settings. A client who writes the template text gets that power.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the name is pasted into the template text.

```python
from flask import Flask, render_template_string, request

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/hello")
def hello():
    name = request.args.get("name", "")
    return render_template_string("<p>Hello, " + name + "</p>")
```

**Compliant:** the template is constant; the name is passed as context and escaped.

```python
from flask import Flask, render_template_string, request

app = Flask(__name__)

PAGE = "<p>Hello, {{ name }}</p>"


@app.route("/hello")
def hello():
    return render_template_string(PAGE, name=request.args.get("name", ""))
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the template constant (a file rendered with `render_template()`, or a constant string) and
  pass request values as context: `render_template_string(PAGE, name=value)`.
- If users choose between templates, pick one from a fixed allow-list.
- If users really must write templates, render them only in Jinja's `SandboxedEnvironment`, and
  pass only the data they need: the sandbox still lets a template use much CPU and memory.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI
- Jinja

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A slice is followed when it slices request data in place (`request.args["tpl"][:200]`),
  a variable assigned request data, or a view parameter; a slice of a value built from request
  data (`(request.args["q"] + "x")[:50]`), or of a variable assigned again after the request value
  (`q = q.strip()`, also `q = q + request.args["b"]` or a fallback `q = request.form["q"]`), is
  missed.
- `from_string()` is checked only on an environment the rule can see: `jinja2.Environment()` or
  `NativeEnvironment()` made in the module or function, Flask's `jinja_env`, a `Jinja2Templates`
  made in the module or function, and Django's `engines[...]` and `Engine`. An environment returned
  by a helper or received as a parameter is missed.
- An allow-list is recognised only as a lookup in a module-level dict of literals assigned to an
  upper-case name that is never changed, or as a ternary of constants; a membership check is not.
- Request sources are recognised by their shape: a Flask `<int:n>` route parameter and a numeric
  Django URL argument still count as request data, and a function whose first parameter is named
  `request` in a Django module is taken for a view.
- A function named like a class-based view's handler (`get`, `post`, ..., `dispatch`) that takes
  `(self, request, ...)` in a Django module is taken for one also outside a class: its parameters
  after `request` count as URL arguments.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/template/template-injection.py`](../../../rules/python/template/template-injection.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/python/template/template-injection.yml`](../../../rules/python/template/template-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
